tagline: East out of Washington Depot on the old Litchfield road.
intro: Route 109 leaves Washington Depot on Bee Brook Road in company with Route 47, and a third of a mile on it splits off east for Morris. From there it runs as Old Litchfield Road for about three miles through a town of rolling hills, mixed woods and open fields.

The town was named for George Washington, who came through several times during the Revolution and, as the saying goes, slept at New Preston in 1781. Joseph Hurlbut settled this eastern side of it in 1734, and his neighborhood took the name Judea Parish.

moments.title: Washington Depot
moments.text: The mill village once called Factory Hollow lost much of its center to the Shepaug flood of August 1955, and a later visit here gave Gilmore Girls its Stars Hollow.

moments.title: Sunny Ridge
moments.text: Ten houses and their barns sit around a triangle of roads that was a stop on the north-south stage and mail route, and where the Rising Sun Tavern took in travelers from 1748.
